page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.1-4 is an entry-tier, compute-oriented virtual instance within the Optimized family. It is based on the x86_64 architecture and operates using an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates one physical core delivering two execution threads, represented as two vCPUs. Compute resources are provisioned with dedicated allocation, preventing neighbor contention and ensuring sustained CPU performance. The instance is outfitted with 4.0 GB of total RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per thread.

The instance architecture omits local storage disks entirely, requiring operators to rely on external block storage solutions for operating system images and persistent file systems. No graphics accelerators are present, limiting acceleration options for parallel math or machine learning pipelines. For external connectivity, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure provisions one complimentary public IPv4 address with this profile. By decoupling persistent storage and hardware accelerators, the resource footprint emphasizes lean processor utilization.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides an economical entry point into dedicated Intel Xeon compute capacity without paying for unneeded memory or peripheral devices. A trade-off of the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio is reduced headroom for memory-intensive in-memory datastores or heavy container virtualization. Consequently, the VM.Optimized3.Flex.1-4 is suited for workloads characterized by moderate CPU demand and limited memory footprint, such as microservices, web reverse proxies, continuous integration worker agents, batch task runners, and standard infrastructure utility servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.1-4 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with two vCPUs derived from a single dedicated physical core of an Intel Xeon 6354 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance pairs dedicated processing power with 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating remote network-attached volumes for persistent data requirements. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, while networking capabilities feature one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because compute resources are fully dedicated rather than shared or burstable, performance remains consistent across execution cycles. This profile delivers cost efficiency for entry-level computational requirements where predictable single-thread execution is needed without the overhead of massive memory allocations. The instance is well matched for lightweight microservices, small CI/CD build nodes, network proxies, and moderate utility workloads.
